 In The Court Of Addl. Sessions Judge (Sftc) :

JUDGMENT 1. Feeling aggrieved from the Judgment dated 17.02.2023 and Order on Sentence dated 01.06.2023 passed by the Ld. MM-04, South West District, Dwarka Courts whereby Ld. MM was pleased to convict the appellant for the offence U/s 279/304A IPC, and awarded a simple imprisonment of two months for offence committed U/s 279 IPC and simple imprisonment of three months for offence U/s 304A IPC which are to be run concurrently.

sentences.text:
BRIEF FACTS:
2. The case of the prosecution is that on 23.02.2018, at around 7:00 PM, the accused person/ appellant namely Om Prakash was driving an RTV bus bearing registration no. DL- 1VC-0240 (herein after shall be referred as "offending vehicle") in a rash and negligent manner and had hit one child namely Ajuba who died as a result of the accident near the red light under Palam Flyover, Dwarka.
Thereafter, the FIR No. 45/2018 U/s 279/304A IPC was registered on 23.02.2018.

After the trial, Ld. MM found the accused/ appellant guilty for offences committed U/s 279/304A Omprakash vs State on 16 March, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/139450694/
1 IPC.
Therefore, the present appeal.
ARGUMENTS:
3. Ld.
Counsel for the appellant argued that the prosecution has failed to prove that accident was caused by the vehicle no. DL-1VC-0240 because no blood stains were found on the offending vehicle.
The prosecution has also failed to prove thta appellant was driving his vehicle in rash and negligent manner or that the said accident was caused by the Appellant.

The witnesses examined by prosecution had deposed that the accused was driving the offending vehicle in a high speed but they have not specifically deposed that accused was driving the offending vehicle in rash and negligent manner.
Mere high speed is not a criteria to prove that the offending vehicle was being driven in rash and negligent manner.
Moreover, PW-1 Sh. Ramdhar and PW-3 Ms. Tamanna Khan did not state the speed of the vehicle.
Furthermore, no skid/ tyre marks have been obtained by the prosecution to indicate that the vehicle was being driven in high speed.
The prosecution has also failed to prove that whether the traffic light was red or not.

Therefore,
prosecution failed to establish whether the pedestrian was within his right to cross the road at the crossing.
Further, site plan does not disclose any traffic signal as to where the traffic light is placed.

4. It is further argued that there are glaring contradictions in the statements of eye-witnesses i.e.
PW-1 Sh. Ramdhar/ father of the deceased and PW-3 Mr. Tamanna Khan. PW-1 made a contradictory statement in his cross-examination with regard to the arrest of accused.
Further PW-1 being illiterate, produced an implanted document with no whereabouts of the person who handed over to him.
Statement of PW-3 recorded U/s 161 Cr. PC was taken on 15.03.2018 i.e. after 20 days of the date of alleged accident.

5. He further argued that During the cross-examination of PW-6 Ct. Harish deposed that there was no zebra crossing and driver cannot run the vehicle in very high speed because of a sharp turn at the spot.

Further, neither the mechanical inspector nor the photographs of the spot taken by the police officials reflect the blood stains under the left front tyre of RTV as alleged by PW-5 (Retd) SI Ajit Singh.
The prosecution has miserably failed to prove its case against the accused.

He has relied upon the following judgments:
A. Ram Chander Vs. State, MANU/DE/6123/2017.

sentences.text: Per Contra, Ld. Chief PP for the State argued that there is no reason of false implication.
The appellant was not known to the father of deceased who is the eye-witness in this Case.

FIR was lodged promptly and in the FIR itself, it is recorded that the number of the offending vehicle was given to the father of the deceased by a passer-by which was immediately handed over to the IO of the case.
Father of the deceased/ PW-1 is illiterate person and was not aware about the legal terminology i.e rash and negligent driving.
He simply stated about the manner in which the accident was caused.
The testimony of PW-1 and PW-3 proves that appellant was driving the offending vehicle in rash and negligent manner and over-run the deceased thereby caused his death.
Therefore, there is no illegality in the judgment of conviction passed by the Ld. Trial Court.
FINDINGS 7.
I have bestowed my thoughtful considerations to the rival submissions made before me.
Accused is indicted for offences u/s 279/304-A IPC.

Section 279 IPC punishes the offence of driving a vehicle in a manner "so rashly or negligently as to endanger human life, or to be likely to cause hurt or injury to any other person" ; and section 304 A IPC provides punishment for causing death of any person by doing any rash or negligent act not amounting to culpable homicide.
8. Proof of rashness and negligence is required for section 279 IPC as also u/s 304 A IPC.
To constitute either of the offences u/s 279 IPC or 304 A IPC, proof of criminal rashness or criminal negligence is essential.

In order to establish criminal liability the facts must be such that the negligence of the accused went beyond a mere matter of compensation and showed such a disregard for life and safety of others as to amount to a crime.
9. In order to bring home the guilt of the accused u/s 279/304-A IPC, prosecution has to prove three aspects, firstly that the accused was driving the offeding vehicle at the time of accident.

Secondly that the said offending vehicle was being driven by the accused in rash or negligent manner causing the accident in question and thirdly, in the said road accident victim Ajuba succumbed to his injuries.
10. In so far as the afore-noted third aspect is concerned, there has not been any serious challenge or dispute on the part of the appellant.
This aspect also stands sufficiently established by MLC Ex. PA-5 and post mortem report Ex. PA-7.
The appellant has not disputed the genuineness of these two documents.

11. The Postmortem report Ex.PA-7 of deceased Ajuba reveals that cause of death of deceased was haemmorage shock due to severe cranio cerebral injury and septicemia consequent upon blood force impact on head due to road traffic accident.
Thus, the evidence available on record is sufficient to prove that Ajuba has died in the accident caused by the offending vehicle.

Omprakash vs State on 16 March, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/139450694/
3 12.

sentences.text: It is worthwhile noting at this juncture that the above noted second aspect of the case that is rashness or negligence on the part of the accused can be deliberated upon only after the prosecution is successful in crossing the initial hurdle of proving first aspect that is the involvement of the offending vehicle as well as the accused to the driver of the same.
To this effect prosecution had examined public witness namely PW-1 Ramdhar and PW-3 Mr. Tamanna Khan who both are eyewitness of the accident.

13. PW-1 Sh. Ramdhar S/o Late Sh. Sumeri Lal deposed as follows:
"The accident happened about 2 1/2 years ago.
Accident happened around festival of Holi.
I do not remember the exact date as I am illiterate and unable to remember the date.
I cannot read and write.
My son Ajuba was going towards the office of Bhawna Goad under Palam flyover and during that time one RTV bus came from the Dwarka side and hit my son from the back side.
Thereafter, my son was taken to the hospital by the public persons.
Name of the accused/ driver was Om Prakash.

The driver/
accused was driving the bus in very high speed.
Police recorded my statement Ex. PW 1/A bearing my thumb impression at point A.
Police prepared site plan at my instance Ex. PW1/B
bearing my thumb impression at point A.
I had handed over a slip on which number of offending vehicle was written to the police and same was seized vide seizure memo Ex. PW 1/C (colly) bearing my thumb impression at point A..."

Mr. Tamanna Khan S/o Safiulla Khan deposed as follows:
"On 23.02.2018, when I was standing near the red light under the Palam Flyover, I saw that one RTV bus coming from the side of Sector-1, Dwarka and taking the U-turn hit one child from backside who was crossing the road.
He rode over the bus on that child and immediately after that he stopped the bus and ran away from the spot.
I did not see the face of the driver.
I dialled the 100 number and informed the police about the accident.
Driver was driving the vehicle in high speed despite the fact that the driver was taking a U-turn.

At this stage, photograph of the offending vehicle bearing registration no.
DL1VC0240 are shown to the witness.
All are already Ex. P1 (colly).
I had stated the registration number of the offending vehicle as mentioned above to the police."
Counsel for appellant argued that no blood stains were found on the offending vehicle.
No photograph of the spot was taken by the IO in compliance of guidelines of Hon'ble High Court of Delhi in Abdul Subhan Vs. State (supra).
Therefore, prosecution fails to prove that the accident was caused by the offending vehicle and appellant was driving the same at the time of accident.
PW-1 and PW-3 both have correctly identified the offending vehicle in the photograph Ex. P1 (colly).
PW-1 has also identified the appellant as the driver of the offending vehicle at the time of accident.
PW-3 has fairly conceeded that he has not seen the face of driver.

Admittedly, as per record, appellant is Omprakash vs State on 16 March, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/139450694/
4 the registered owner of the offending vehicle.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: A notice U/s 133 MV Act was served to appellant.
In the reply to the said notice, appellant has admitted that he was driving the offending vehicle at the time of accident.
Moreover, as per the seizure memo of the offending vehicle, the offending vehicle was found at the spot of accident unattended because appellant had run away after causing the accident.
Appellant had failed to explain why he left the offending vehicle unattended at the spot of accident if the accident was not caused by him.
The appellant did not lead any evidence to prove that accident was not cause by the offending vehicle and he was not the driver of it at the time of accident.

After appreciation of oral testimony of PW-1 and PW-3, this Court is of the considered opinion that it has been proved beyond the reasonable doubt that the accident was caused by offending vehicle and it was being driven by the appellant at the time of accident.
16. To prove the rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle by the appellant, the prosecution has again relied upon the oral testimony of PW-1 and PW-3.
Ld. Counsel for appellant argued that there was no zebra-crossing.
PW-3 deposed that offending vehicle was not being driven in zig-zag manner.
The speed of the offending vehicle has not been disclosed by PW-1 and PW-3 to prove that it was being driven at very high speed.
17. PW-1 and PW-3 have deposed that offending vehicle came from Dwarka side as disclosed in the site plan.
PW-1 deposed that offending vehicle hit his son from the back side.
PW-3 deposed that offending vehicle while taking U-turn hit one child from the back side who was crossing the road and it was run over on the said child.
The site plan Ex. PW1/B also corroborates the testimony of PW-1 and PW-3.
It is shown in the site plan that the offending vehicle was coming from Dwarka side and accident was caused at point A, after the offending vehicle took a U-turn.
PW-1 and PW-3 have categorically deposed the manner in which the offending vehicle was being driven and the accident was caused.
PW-1 is an illiterate person who cannot read and write.
Therefore, it is not expected from an illiterate person to have knowledge about the legal terminology i.e. rashness and negligence.
He, in his simple language, has explained the manner in which the accident was caused.

18. In the case of Alister Anthony Pareira Vs. State of Maharashtra (2012) 2 SCC 648, the Hon'ble Apex Court of India has made observations with regard to the applicability of law U/s 304A IPC and 304 Part-II IPC in road accident cases as follows:

entities.text: Alister Anthony Pareira Vs. State of Maharashtra (2012) 2 SCC 648
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: " 45. In Prabhakaran Vs. State of Kerala14, this Court was concerned with the appeal filed by a convict who was found guilty of the offence punishable under Section 304 Part II IPC.
In that case, the bus driven by the convict ran over a boy aged 10 years.

The prosecution case was that bus was being driven by the appellant therein at the enormous speed and although the passengers had cautioned the driver to stop as they had seen children crossing the road in a queue, the driver ran over the student on his head.
It was alleged that the driver had real intention to cause death of persons to whom harm may be caused on the bus hitting them.
He was charged with offence punishable under Section 302 IPC.

The Trial Court found that no 14 2007 (14) SCC 269 intention had been proved in the case but at the same time the accused acted with the knowledge that it was likely to cause death, and, therefore, convicted the accused of culpable homicide not amounting to murder punishable under Section Omprakash vs State on 16 March, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/139450694/
5 304 Part II IPC and sentenced him to undergo rigorous imprisonment for five years and pay a fine of Rs.15,000/- with a default sentence of imprisonment for three years.

entities.text: Section Omprakash vs State on 16 March
entities.label: PROVISION

sentences.text: The High Court dismissed the appeal and the matter reached this Court.

While observing that Section 304A speaks of causing death by negligence and applies to rash and negligent acts and does not apply to cases where there is an intention to cause death or knowledge that the act will in all probability cause death and that Section 304A only applies to cases in which without any such intention or knowledge death is caused by a rash and negligent act, on the factual scenario of the case, it was held that the appropriate conviction would be under Section 304A IPC and not Section 304 Part II IPC.

Prabhakaran14 does not say in absolute terms that in no case of an automobile accident that results in death of a person due to rash and negligent act of the driver, the conviction can be maintained for the offence under Section 304 Part II IPC even if such act (rash or negligent) was done with the knowledge that by such act of his, death was likely to be caused.
Prabhakaran14 turned on its own facts.
Each case obviously has to be decided on its own facts.

In a case where negligence or rashness is the cause of death and nothing more, Section 304A may be attracted but where the rash or negligent act is preceded with the knowledge that such act is likely to cause death, Section 304 Part II IPC may be attracted and if such a rash and negligent act is preceded by real intention on the part of the wrong doer to cause death, offence may be punishable under Section 302 IPC.

46. On behalf of the appellant it was strenuously urged that the conviction of the appellant by the High Court for the offence under Section 304 Part II IPC rests solely on the premise that the appellant had knowledge that his reckless or negligent driving in a drunken condition could result in serious consequences of causing fatal accident .

It was submitted that neither in the charge framed against the appellant,
the crux of the prosecution case that the appellant was in a drunken condition was stated nor incriminating evidences and circumstances relating to rashness or negligence of the accused in the drunken condition were put to him in the statement under Section 313 of the Code."
19.
In this case also, the appellant while driving offending vehicle i.e. RTV/ commercial vehicle should have been more vigilant while driving the commercial vehicle on road.
He overrun a boy aged about 15 years who was crossing the road while taking U-turn and caused his death.
Even if there was no zebra crossing for a pedestrian to cross the road, the appellant was behind the wheel and has full control over the brakes of the offending vehicle.

Appellant simply cannot be exonerated from his liability mere on the ground that police had conducted shoddy investigation if there is sufficient material available on record to prove his rash and negligent driving.
Instead of taking the deceased to the hospital after the accident, appellant had run away from there leaving behind the offending vehicle.

20. In view of the above discussion, the Court is of the considered opinion that the prosecution has been able to prove its case against the appellant beyond reasonable doubt that accident has been caused due to rash and negligent driving of offending vehicle by the appellant in which master Ajuba Omprakash vs State on 16 March, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/139450694/
6 lost his life.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Therefore the judgment of conviction of appellant for the offences under Section 279/304-A IPC is upheld and accordingly, the appeal filed by appellant is dismissed.
21. On the aspect of quantum of sentence, Ld. Counsel for appellant argued that the appellant is the sole bread earner of the family.
His old age parents and wife are suffering from various ailments.
He has two sons who are studying in 6th and 12th class.
He is a first time offender.
The family of deceased has already been granted compensation of Rs. 16 Lakhs by the MACT Court.
Therefore, it is prayed that lenient view be taken against the appellant 22.
On the other hand, Ld. Addl. PP for the State has argued that the Ld. Trial Court has already taken the lenient view against the appellant.
Therefore, the sentence awarded by Ld. Trial Court does not need any interference.
23. The Ld. Trial Court had awarded simple imprisonement of two months for the offence U/s 279 IPC and simple imprisonment for three months for the offence U/s 304A IPC.
It has been directed that both the sentences shall run concurrently.
24. The appellant had run away from the spot after causing the accident.
He was driving a commercial vehicle and should have been more vigilant while plying the RTV on the road.
It is not the case that accident was caused with any other vehicle rather, he ran over a pedestrian.

The Ld.
Trial Court had already taken very lenient view while passing the order on sentence.
Therefore, the sentence awarded by the ld.
Trial Court does not warrants any interference and the sentence awrded by the Ld. Trial Court is upheld.
Appellant is taken into custody to serve the sentence awarded to him.
Accordingly, the present appeal is disposed off.
25. Copy of this judgment be provided free of cost to the appellants.
Copy of the judgment along with the Trial Court Record be sent to the ld. Trial Court concerned for information and compliance.
26. Appeal file be consigned to record room after compliance of necessary legal formalities.
